news.title: Canada Builds an Energy Exit From the U.S.
news.summary: Canada is building an energy export industry for a world beyond the tariff-chasing United States. In 2024, the U.S. bought all but 0.01% of Canada’s natural gas exports. Ottawa now wants 55% of those exports to go to other countries by the mid-2030s, and Germany’s state-owned Uniper has signed a 20-year deal for liquefied natural gas from a planned British Columbia terminal. Prime Minister Mark Carney has fast-tracked a state-backed pipeline to carry 1 million barrels a day of Alberta crude to the Pacific coast for Asian buyers, and…

analysis.summary: Canada is fast-tracking a 1M bpd Pacific crude pipeline and LNG deals to diversify energy exports away from the U.S. toward Asia and Europe.
analysis.rationale: Rerouting future Canadian crude and gas exports shifts regional trade flows rather than clearly altering net global crude supply or demand in the near term.

news.title: Guyana Oil Boom Rekindles Frontier Drilling Appetite
news.summary: Exxon announced this week that total oil production in Guyana had topped 1 million barrels. Guyana’s transformation into a formidable oil power is now motivating other oil majors to seek opportunities to replicate Exxon’s story. It is quite easy to see why. Exxon, along with its partners Hess Corp. and CNOOC, spent billions on developing the Stabroek Block offshore the tiny South American country. The investment paid off with a string of discoveries opening up resources estimated at over 11 billion barrels of crude. With this year’s…

analysis.summary: Exxon's Guyana oil output has exceeded 1M bpd, spurring other oil majors to pursue frontier drilling opportunities.
analysis.rationale: Rising non-OPEC production in Guyana and renewed frontier exploration appetite point to higher global crude supply, creating downward price pressure.

news.title: EU Moves to Overhaul Emergency Oil Stockpiles
news.summary: The European Union wants countries to stockpile the fuels they actually use, following a nine-month Middle East conflict that has exposed a problem with Europe's emergency oil reserves: having enough oil in storage doesn't necessarily mean having enough diesel or jet fuel. The European Commission is preparing changes that would require member states to align their emergency reserves more closely with national fuel consumption and refining capacity, according to a draft seen by Bloomberg on Thursday. Under existing rules, EU countries must maintain…

analysis.summary: The EU plans to overhaul emergency reserve rules so member states align stockpiles with national fuel consumption and refining capacity.
analysis.rationale: Rebalancing reserves toward refined products like diesel and jet fuel could alter product-level demand, but the net directional impact on crude oil prices is ambiguous from the summary.

news.title: Trafigura Not Rushing to Alternative Marine Fuels
news.summary: Shipowners have been ordering vessels capable of burning alternative fuels, but Trafigura’s marine fuel business isn't seeing enough demand for those fuels to justify major new investments. The ships may have different engines, but much of the fuel going into them hasn't changed. “We will not make any big alternative-fuel investments until there's demand,” Kenneth Dam, executive director of TFG Marine, told Reuters at a conference in Geneva on Thursday. Trafigura owns 70% of TFG Marine, with tanker owners Frontline and CMB.Each…

analysis.summary: Trafigura's marine fuel arm sees insufficient demand for alternative marine fuels to justify major investments, as vessels continue burning conventional fuels.
analysis.rationale: Delayed adoption of alternative marine fuels preserves conventional petroleum bunker demand, offering modest support to oil demand.

news.title: Trump’s Ukraine Energy Truce Unravels as Russian Missiles Hit Kyiv
news.summary: Politics, Geopolitics & Conflict Trump’s October “energy truce” between Russia and Ukraine in October is over, and Vladimir Putin has taken a new one off the table. After meeting Trump and Xi at the APEC summit on Thursday, Putin said Russia would not negotiate after Ukraine’s strikes on the Crimean Bridge. Russia hit Kyiv with ballistic missiles and drones Friday morning, killing at least three people, damaging three bridges and a critical infrastructure facility, and forcing power cuts in the capital and three western…

analysis.summary: Russia-Ukraine energy truce collapses as Putin rules out talks and Russia strikes Kyiv infrastructure.
analysis.rationale: The breakdown of the energy truce and renewed missile strikes on critical infrastructure heighten geopolitical risk and potential energy supply disruptions.

news.title: Iraq's Oil Crackdown Sparks New Showdown With Kurdistan
news.summary: Iraq’s federal government is using its oil-smuggling case against the pro-Iranian militia Kata’ib Hezbollah south of Baghdad to force the Kurdistan Regional Government in the north to hand over more oil and open its fields to federal inspectors. South of Baghdad, the Iraqi PM has ordered federal forces to take over a pipeline at Jurf al-Sakhar (Babil province) that the pro-Iranian militia has been illegally tapping into since at least 2021. Iraqi officials estimate the group made away with hundreds of millions of dollars in crude. Baghdad…

analysis.summary: Baghdad orders federal takeover of a militia-tapped pipeline and pressures Kurdistan over oil fields and smuggling.
analysis.rationale: The snippet describes an internal Iraqi political and security confrontation without enough detail to determine whether net crude supply will rise or fall.

news.title: WTI Crude Sinks More Than 5% as Global Oil Glut Fears Grow
news.summary: The oil market spent the week weighing an increase in global supply against the risk of further disruptions in the Middle East. More crude is reaching buyers from the region, while U.S. inventories are building. Attacks on tankers and energy infrastructure remain a threat, but they have not been enough to stop the decline in prices. For now, the supply story appears to be winning. January West Texas Intermediate crude oil futures are down more than 5% for the week. The decline suggests traders are putting more weight on the barrels reaching the…

analysis.summary: WTI crude falls over 5% on the week as rising global supply and U.S. inventory builds outweigh Middle East risks.
analysis.rationale: Increasing barrels reaching buyers and building U.S. inventories point to oversupply, directly pressuring crude prices downward.

news.title: Iran Steps Up Hormuz Tanker Attacks as Oil Prices Slide
news.summary: Iran has intensified attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz in recent weeks, just as crude oil flows from the Persian Gulf recover and oil prices fall amid expectations of oversupply within months. The number of attacks soared in October to the highest level since the Iran war began at the end of February, and has continued at nearly daily occurrences so far in November, according to data compiled by Bloomberg. Meanwhile, crude oil volumes flowing from the Strait of Hormuz have declined in recent days, although it’s unclear if this is…

analysis.summary: Iran intensifies Strait of Hormuz tanker attacks and recent flows dip, even as Persian Gulf supply recovers and oversupply fears weigh on prices.
analysis.rationale: Escalating tanker attacks and a recent flow dip are bullish disruption risks, but recovering Gulf flows and oversupply expectations exert bearish pressure.

news.title: Iran Refuses Nuclear Inspections as U.S. Military Threats Mount
news.summary: Iran has warned once again that it would not grant access to its nuclear sites and materials to UN inspectors amid continued U.S. threats of military strikes, a senior Iranian official was quoted as saying on Friday. “We will not accept being bombed on the one hand while being asked in a tone of entitlement, on the other, to provide detailed information about our materials and sites and grant unrestricted access to them,” Reza Najafi, Iran’s ambassador to international organizations in Vienna, told the International Atomic…

analysis.summary: Iran refuses UN nuclear inspections amid ongoing U.S. military strike threats.
analysis.rationale: Heightened U.S.-Iran confrontation over nuclear inspections increases the Middle East geopolitical risk premium for crude oil.

news.title: China’s Solar Exports Surge 21% as U.S. Tariff Deadline Looms
news.summary: Chinese exports of solar cells jumped in October for the second consecutive month as importers are stocking up ahead of new U.S. tariffs on polysilicon coming into effect on December 4. China’s solar cell exports soared by 21% year-over-year to 1.55 billion units in October, Bloomberg reported on Friday, citing data from China’s General Administration of Customs. October was the second month in a row in which Chinese solar cell shipments overseas rose from a year earlier, after four consecutive months of declines between May and August…

analysis.summary: China's solar cell exports jumped 21% YoY in October ahead of a December 4 U.S. polysilicon tariff deadline.
analysis.rationale: Front-running of solar panel trade ahead of U.S. tariffs has no clear direct directional implication for near-term crude oil prices.

news.title: A24 is having a great year at the box office. That could give HBO Max a streaming edge
news.summary: A24 films "Backrooms," "The Drama" and the Elizabeth Holmes documentary, "You Can See Everything," are fueling a banner year at the box office.

analysis.summary: A24's strong box office year may bolster HBO Max's streaming position.
analysis.rationale: Entertainment and media streaming performance is unrelated to crude oil supply, demand, or pricing.

news.title: US Data Center Boom Faces a New Political Reality
news.summary: Starting in January, Democratic governors will lead US states that together hold 77% of the 300 gigawatts (GW) of data center capacity announced for 2027-2030, including the five largest markets: Texas, Virginia, Pennsylvania, Ohio and Georgia. Most of the winning candidates campaigned on making data centers pay their grid costs, rather than on stopping them, so the midterms are likely to change the terms of growth more than its pace. Our risked forecast expects 121 GW to be added in 2027-2030, including about 49 GW of the 191 GW planned for 2029-30.…

news.summary: Japan plans to buy up to 8 million barrels of Saudi crude for the national petroleum reserve it drew down during the Hormuz crisis, under a deal the two countries announced on Friday that makes the purchases subject to favorable market conditions. The deal also gives Saudi Arabia temporary use of an additional 16 million barrels of storage capacity in Japan, expanding the 8 million barrels it already holds there, and the kingdom has begun refilling those tanks, Bloomberg reported. news.summary: The total number of active drilling rigs for oil and gas in the United States rose this week, according to new data that Baker Hughes published on Friday, with the total rig count in the US rising to 607, up 53 from this same time last year. The number of active oil rigs rose by 6 to 469 during the latest reporting period, according to the data. This is 50 above this same time last year. news.summary: Europe’s biggest airline group, Lufthansa, plans to eliminate as many as 1,000 jobs and reduce capacity on short and medium-haul destinations, Bloomberg reported on Friday, citing a letter to employees it had seen. Lufthansa and all other airlines have struggled this year with increasing pressure on profits from soaring fuel prices amid the Middle East conflict. news.summary: The 2026 midterm elections produced a major political shift in Washington. Democrats will control both chambers of Congress when the new session begins in January, during President Donald Trump’s final two years in the White House. That combination almost guarantees more conflict over energy policy, but it does not necessarily mean sweeping changes in federal law. The more consequential changes may occur somewhere else. news.summary: US President Donald Trump, Chinese leader Xi Jinping, and Russian President Vladimir Putin held a historic meeting on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen that delivered modest wins for all three men but no game-changing accords.
